concepts.def: The interaction of a community of living organisms (biotic) with the non-living (abiotic) parts of their environment.
The place where an organism lives. It supplies the conditions and the materials the organism needs from its surroundings in order to survive and reproduce.
All the organisms of one species living in a habitat. A population is the level of organisation between the individual organism and the community.
The populations of all the different species living together in a habitat. Within a community each species depends on the other species living there.

Organisms of the same or different species competing for the same resource where the supply is limited. Plants in a community or habitat often compete with each other for light and space, and for water and mineral ions from the soil. Animals often compete with each other for food, mates and territory.
Within a community each species depends on other species for food, shelter, pollination, seed dispersal etc. If one species is removed it can affect the whole community.
A community where all the species and environmental factors are in balance so that population sizes remain fairly constant.

A non-living factor which can affect a community. The abiotic factors are: light intensity; temperature; moisture levels; soil pH and mineral content; wind intensity and direction; carbon dioxide levels for plants; oxygen levels for aquatic animals.

A living factor which can affect a community. The biotic factors are: availability of food; new predators arriving; new pathogens; one species outcompeting another so the numbers are no longer sufficient to breed.
A feature that an organism has which enables it to survive in the conditions in which it normally lives.

The three types of adaptation. Structural adaptations are features of the organism's body, such as its shape or covering. Behavioural adaptations are things the organism does. Functional adaptations are the ways processes inside the organism's body work.
An organism that lives in an environment that is very extreme, such as at high temperature, pressure, or salt concentration. Bacteria living in deep sea vents are extremophiles.

concepts.term: Materials required to survive and reproduce
concepts.def: To survive and reproduce, organisms require a supply of materials from their surroundings and from the other living organisms there, for example light, water and mineral ions for a plant, and food from other organisms for an animal.

mcqs.q: Which description matches a community in an ecosystem?
options: The populations of every species in a habitat
The individuals of one species in a habitat
The living and non-living parts of a habitat
The non-living conditions present in a habitat
mcqs.explain: A community is the populations of all the different species living together in a habitat; the ecosystem is the interaction of that community with the non-living parts of the environment.

mcqs.q: A gardener sows seedlings very close together in fertile, well-watered soil in an open bed. Which pair of resources will these plants mainly compete for as they grow?
options: Light and mineral ions in the soil
Food and territory around each plant
Mates and shelter from other plants
Food and water taken up from the soil
mcqs.explain: Plants in a community or habitat often compete with each other for light and space, and for water and mineral ions from the soil, and crowded seedlings shade each other and draw on the same soil.

mcqs.q: A disease kills nearly all the insects that pollinate several plant species in a woodland. Which outcome best shows interdependence in this community?
options: Other woodland species are unaffected by it
Many other species in the woodland are affected
Plants are unaffected as they feed themselves
Nothing changes as the community is stable
mcqs.explain: This is interdependence: each species depends on other species for food, shelter, pollination, seed dispersal etc., so if one species is removed it can affect the whole community.

mcqs.q: Which statement describes a stable community?
options: Population sizes remain exactly the same each year
The species stop competing for food and territory
Species and environmental factors are in balance
The abiotic factors in this habitat remain constant
mcqs.explain: A stable community is one where all the species and environmental factors are in balance so that population sizes remain fairly constant.

mcqs.q:
The table shows the mean number of mayfly nymphs collected at four sites along one river.

Site | Dissolved oxygen in mg/dm3 | Mean number of nymphs per sample
W | 9.8 | 42
X | 8.1 | 35
Y | 5.4 | 12
Z | 3.2 | 2

Which conclusion about an abiotic factor is supported by these data?
options: Dissolved oxygen is a biotic factor for the nymphs
Nymph numbers are constant in the whole river
Other river species are unaffected by low oxygen
Fewer nymphs were found where oxygen was lower
mcqs.explain: The data show the mean number of nymphs falling from 42 to 2 as dissolved oxygen falls from 9.8 to 3.2 mg/dm3, so this abiotic factor, oxygen levels for aquatic animals, is linked to the size of the population.

mcqs.q:
The table shows the numbers of a predator and of its prey counted in the same community over four years.

Year | Number of prey | Number of predators
1 | 1200 | 30
2 | 900 | 45
3 | 600 | 60
4 | 800 | 40

Which statement is best supported by these data?
options: Predators and prey compete for the same food
Numbers stayed constant in a stable community
Other species were unaffected by the change
Prey numbers fell as predator numbers rose
mcqs.explain: From year 1 to year 3 the prey fell from 1200 to 600 while the predators rose from 30 to 60, and in year 4 the prey rose as the predators fell, showing how a change in a biotic factor affects the community.

mcqs.q: Rats reach an island on a ship and begin to eat the eggs of a ground-nesting bird. Which biotic factor does this describe?
options: One species outcompeting another species
A new predator arriving in this community
A drop in the soil's moisture levels
A change in the temperature of this island
mcqs.explain: New predators arriving is one of the biotic (living) factors which can affect a community, and the rats are feeding on the birds' eggs.

mcqs.q: Camels live in hot deserts. Which of these is a behavioural adaptation of a camel to desert conditions?
options: It has thick fat stored in a hump on its back
It makes small amounts of concentrated urine
It rests in the shade during the hottest hours
It has long eyelashes to keep out the sand
mcqs.explain: Adaptations may be structural, behavioural or functional, and resting in shade is something the camel does, so it is a behavioural adaptation that helps it survive in the conditions in which it normally lives.

mcqs.q: Bacteria that live in deep sea vents are described as extremophiles. Why?
options: They live in seawater that is warmer than average
They survive by moving away from the hottest water
They tolerate the extreme heat for short periods
They live in water of extreme heat and pressure
mcqs.explain: Some organisms live in environments that are very extreme, such as at high temperature, pressure, or salt concentration, and these organisms are called extremophiles; bacteria living in deep sea vents are extremophiles.
